attacks.claim: The offline expiry guard only catches a device clock set earlier than the server time stored at download. A clock that is behind real time, or set back to any point between download and valid_until, still shows an expired avalanche rating in color as current. This breaks the agreed rule that the app never presents stale safety information as current.
attacks.evidence: "The expiry rule above applies on-device using device time... if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired." QA has only a row for a clock moved earlier than download time. ABSENT: a case for a clock between download time and valid_until.

attacks.claim: Rollback does not reliably remove stale ratings from phones. The flag is read only on next foreground, and the on-device purge is described as running on next launch in QA. A backgrounded or offline phone that is resumed, not relaunched, keeps colored forecast data, so the claim that no stale ratings remain is unsupported.
attacks.evidence: "Set `avalanche_layer=false` (remote config, takes effect on next app foreground)... so no stale ratings remain on phones." vs QA: "offline forecast data purged on next launch | Pass"

attacks.claim: Removing a single center does not purge its offline copies. Those copies keep showing colored ratings until valid_until, which can be many hours after the center asks for removal or revokes permission. The plan has no faster retraction path, and no QA row tests the removal.
attacks.evidence: "its zones disappear within 10 min and any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`"

attacks.claim: The blog post and the public 'Free for everyone' claim are irreversible public commitments scheduled for 10:00 Nov 23 with no hold or retraction condition. The flag can hide the layer but cannot unpublish the post, and the plan does not say what happens if the flag is rolled back after the post is live.
attacks.evidence: "Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check that all 19 centers render." / "Free for everyone."

attacks.claim: The pre-publication gate is only 'a check' with no criteria, owner, or QA row. The layer reaches 100% of users at 08:00, two hours before the post and card, so the check that gates the public launch is unevidenced.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%. Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check that all 19 centers render." (QA table contains no such check)

attacks.claim: The poll-success alert only confirms that a poll completed. A partial or malformed WADE response, such as missing centers or a schema change, counts as success while ratings are wrong or absent. No content validation or per-center-count alert is defined.
attacks.evidence: "Pages Maps on-call: no successful poll for 30 min, any center not updated for 26 h during its season..." (ABSENT: validation of poll content or alert on centers returned per poll)

attacks.claim: The origin rate limit is per IP at 120 req/min, but the app requests per visible tile and CDN hits are not counted. Shared-NAT and carrier IPs can be throttled on cache misses, and 429 responses have no specified client retry or backoff and no alert.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP (CDN-cached responses are not counted)" (ABSENT: client handling of 429 and alerting on rate-limit responses)

attacks.claim: The 92% hit rate is unsupported. Arbitrary bbox values make each pan or zoom a distinct cache key, so the real hit rate is likely far lower. Cache misses then go to origin, where autoscaling is capped at 6 instances with no per-instance capacity figure, and no degradation path is stated for a weekend or storm spike.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" with "92% CDN hit rate"; "origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances"

attacks.claim: The 08:00 flip to 100% and the 10:00 blog post hit a possibly cold CDN, and no load test or launch-traffic capacity evidence appears in the QA summary, so origin saturation and 5xx alerts are likely at launch.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%." (ABSENT: load test or launch-traffic capacity evidence)

attacks.claim: The 'expires them on time' guarantee depends on client-side enforcement because no CDN TTL is stated for /avy/v1/zones. A cached response can carry a forecast past valid_until, and the artifact does not say it is purged on expiry.
attacks.evidence: "our API keeps serving forecasts still inside `valid_until` and expires them on time"; ABSENT: CDN cache TTL or purge-on-expiry for `/avy/v1/zones`

attacks.claim: The agreement permits display in the app, but an unauthenticated, CDN-cached public endpoint serving the same ratings to any client looks like redistribution beyond in-app display. The artifact does not show the agreement allows that.
attacks.evidence: "display in our app is permitted for free and paid users" vs "read-only, unauthenticated … and serves only WADE public data."

attacks.claim: The artifact says ratings come from the issuing centers, but the only agreement cited is one WADE contract. It does not show that all 19 centers have authorized display and attribution under C-2209, or that they have no separate terms, while the blog post publicly commits to all 19.
attacks.evidence: "ratings come only from the issuing centers under a signed data agreement" vs "WADE data agreement signed 2026-09-30 (contract C-2209)"; ABSENT: per-center license scope. "Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers"

attacks.claim: The zone color and label are derived from the highest of three bands. The agreement bars altering ratings, and legal's review covers card text and terms, not this aggregation against C-2209.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three" alongside "may not alter ratings or forecast text"; ABSENT: legal sign-off on the aggregated zone rating

attacks.claim: The 'no location sent' claim is too narrow. Viewport bbox requests plus IP addresses in server and CDN logs can reveal where a user is, and the artifact states no retention or log handling for them and no privacy policy or data-inventory update.
attacks.evidence: "device location is not sent" and "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" (ABSENT: log retention for IP and bbox data; privacy policy update)

attacks.claim: The screen-reader check covers only a current zone. Expired and no-forecast zones are where stale safety information could reach a screen-reader user, and their spoken output is never specified or tested.
attacks.evidence: VoiceOver / TalkBack: zone announced as "[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]" | Pass. (ABSENT: spoken output for 'Forecast expired' and 'No current forecast')

attacks.claim: WADE is the sole upstream for all 19 centers, and the artifact describes no continuity path if the feed or contract C-2209 changes or ends.
attacks.evidence: "Our backend polls WADE every 10 min" (ABSENT: fallback to direct center feeds, C-2209 termination terms, or an exit plan)

attacks.claim: The CDN budget alert at $400/month has no linked action or cap, so spend is unbounded during a surge. The origin cost estimate also lacks the assumptions needed to verify it.
attacks.evidence: "CDN budget alert at $400/month; origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances." "origin cost ~$140/month"

attacks.claim: The no-forecast rule is written in terms of issuance date, but expiry uses valid_until. A forecast issued before today and still valid is ambiguous under the current wording.
attacks.evidence: "Zones with no current forecast (out of season, or none issued today)"

attacks.claim: The terms-of-use update is a public change with no publish date, so its timing relative to the flag and the blog post is unknown.
attacks.evidence: "Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)." (no publish date)

attacks.claim: No size cap is stated for offline forecast and geometry storage per device or per download.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any size limit on stored offline forecast data

attacks.claim: Removing a center depends on a config edit whose deploy path is not described. The on-device purge is also described two ways (next launch vs. deleted on rollback).
attacks.evidence: "editing `config/avy_centers.json`... zones disappear within 10 min" vs "purged on next launch"

attacks.claim: Several separable changes (layer, card, blog post, analytics, endpoint, offline storage) ship under one change ID, which makes independent rollback and review harder.
attacks.evidence: "Change: RM-6120" with layer, card, blog post, endpoint, and offline storage bundled

attacks.claim: Success is not defined beyond dashboard uptime and crash-free sessions, so the team cannot tell whether the layer meets its safety purpose. Gray zones may also make the map look empty for most of the year.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any usage or user-need success metric. "Zones with no current forecast... show a gray hatched fill"
